common_name: Graf Zeppelin Garden Phlox (White Red-Eyed Classic Tall Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun; this historic European-bred selection benefits from generous spacing to keep foliage dry and limit powdery mildew.

directions: Graf Zeppelin is a historic European-bred garden phlox valued for its clean white, saucer-shaped flowers centered by a small carmine-red eye, carried in large, rounded clusters atop sturdy, upright stems. It typically reaches a traditional full garden-phlox height and benefits from generous spacing to keep foliage dry and reduce powdery mildew in humid climates. Plant divisions in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous bloom. The fragrant midsummer flowers attract butterflies and hummingbirds and pair well with other classic cottage-garden perennials.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Düsterlohe Garden Phlox (Deep Wine-Red Classic Tall Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing generously for airflow; this old German-bred selection is grown for its unusually deep, saturated flower color.

directions: Düsterlohe (German for roughly 'dark flame') is an old European garden phlox selection prized for its intensely saturated, wine-red to magenta flowers held in dense, rounded clusters on sturdy stems. Its richly colored blooms rank among the deepest reds found in traditional garden phlox and make a dramatic accent against lighter-colored perennials. Grow it in full sun in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil, spacing plants well apart for airflow to limit powdery mildew, a common issue on densely planted garden phlox in humid regions. Deadhead after the first flush to encourage rebloom and divide every three to four years to keep clumps vigorous.
sources: Mt. Cuba Center Phlox paniculata Trial Report

common_name: Widar Garden Phlox (Violet-Blue White-Star-Eyed Classic Tall Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun with ample spacing; this classic European-bred selection is grown for its two-toned violet-blue flowers with a pale starry center.

directions: Widar is a classic European-bred garden phlox noted for its soft violet-blue petals surrounding a contrasting pale, star-shaped center, giving each flower a distinctive two-toned appearance. Large, rounded flower clusters appear atop sturdy, upright stems in midsummer and are reliably fragrant, drawing butterflies and hummingbirds to the garden. Plant in full sun in fertile, evenly moist, well-drained soil with ample spacing between plants to promote airflow and reduce susceptibility to powdery mildew. Lift and divide clumps every few years in early spring to maintain a healthy, floriferous habit.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
